content.thinking:
I notice the error rate during the incident (1.0%) actually sat below the 1.2% baseline, so there was no elevated error rate — this was purely a latency incident. The restart at 18:23:13 and the recovery at 18:24:05 line up closely, but that's correlation, not confirmed causation; I still need to dig into why pricing slowed in the first place.

I never actually inspected io-pricing's own metrics or logs directly — I only inferred its state from io-shop's logs, and no deploys or flag changes turned up as explanations either. I should be careful not to overstate any computed figures as certain, describe things qualitatively (errors stayed within baseline, impact was latency-only), and keep the executive summary generic, referring to "the online shop's account pages" rather than naming components, while staying concise but complete.

assumptions: That restarting io-pricing is what ended the slowdown. The restart was issued at 18:23:13 and the service was seen at baseline at 18:24:05, but the metrics place recovery at 18:24 and no control comparison was made; the timing is consistent with the restart working, and also consistent with the dependency recovering on its own.

That io-pricing was the faulty component. This was inferred entirely from io-shop's own logs and the service register; io-pricing's metrics, logs and deploy history were never queried, and no deploy/change data was pulled for it.

That the slow dependency, rather than anything in io-shop, caused the latency. Supported by the absence of io-shop deploys in the 143 minutes before 18:23 and no recent flag changes, but no change data was examined outside those windows.

That the elevated error lines in the logs (ClientDisconnected on the account page) reflect shoppers abandoning slow pages rather than a server-side failure mode. Note that these disconnects were already appearing at 18:14-18:16, before the recorded onset at 18:17 and before the first slow-upstream warning, and that the measured error rate during the incident did not exceed the pre-incident baseline.
That the alternative explanation - a third-party rather than internally owned pricing service - is ruled out. This rests on the service register being accurate; it was not independently verified.

That the onset was 18:17. That is where the latency signature begins, but the account-page disconnect warnings start at least three minutes earlier, so the true start of customer impact may be earlier than the window the impact figures were measured over.
That the proposed draft pull request addresses the cause. It was filed after mitigation and its contents were not reviewed as part of this response.
input.executive_summary: For roughly seven minutes on the evening of 26 September 2026, the account page of the online shop was very slow: pages that normally came back in well under half a second took around a second and a half, because an internal service the shop relies on to calculate basket totals started responding slowly. Shoppers loading their account page during that window saw long waits, and some gave up and closed the page before it finished loading. Requests were not, on the whole, failing more often than usual — the error rate over the incident window was no higher than the level seen before it started — so the customer harm here was slowness and abandonment rather than outright failures. The automated responder picked the alert up about five minutes after the slowdown began, traced the delay to the basket-total service, restarted that service, and confirmed the shop was back to its normal response times shortly afterwards. A draft code change was subsequently proposed for review. The underlying reason the basket-total service slowed down has not yet been identified, so a recurrence cannot be ruled out until it is.
input.root_cause: Calls from io-shop to its internal pricing dependency (pricing.io-internal.svc, owned by checkout-platform) began returning consistently in ~1500ms from 18:17, which dominated io-shop's request latency (p50/p95/p99 rose from roughly 45/220/380ms to 1545/1715/1890ms) and led some shoppers to abandon the account page mid-request; no io-shop deploy, release or feature-flag change was recorded in the window. Why io-pricing itself slowed down was never established — no one looked at io-pricing's own metrics or logs — so this identifies the failing component, not the underlying defect.
